notes: Dev-split ABox revision that carries inverse (successor_of is the inverse of predecessor_of). The edit makes Windows 95 the direct predecessor of Windows Vista (originally Windows XP), a stored fact stated in Vista's Wikipedia lead. Related near asks the inverse as a yes/no question ('Was Windows 95 the direct predecessor of Windows Vista?', no then yes). An open question from Windows 95's side ('which version directly succeeded Windows 95?') was dropped after review: predecessor_of is not functional (the Windows line branched), so after the edit both Windows 98 and Windows Vista would be fair answers; the yes/no form needs no uniqueness. The paraphrase says 'successor' rather than 'predecessor' so it does not duplicate the inverse question. Related far binds the subject through its development code name Longhorn, a separate fact every account of Vista repeats; the original answer is stored under that name (Longhorn was announced as the successor to XP). The three derived queries follow the edit to the new predecessor and look up a fact about it that is not in its name: its development code name (Whistler to Chicago), whether it introduced the Start menu (no to yes) and whether it was built on the Windows NT kernel (yes to no), so one yes/no item flips each way. The release year was dropped as a composition because 'Windows 95' names it. Near unrelated: Vista's own successor (Windows 7), which the edit leaves alone; a model that blends Vista into Windows 95 would answer Windows 98. successor_of is also the edited relation of no other dev record now (technology-replace-d004 moved to based_on).
